reasons: Both answers diagnose the problem the same way and ship nearly identical server-spherecast plus client-rendered designs that meet every rubric item. B is somewhat more robust: when the server rejects a cast, it tells the caster to remove the predicted visual; it caps active projectiles per player, validates input more thoroughly, sends an explicit end event when a fireball misses, and filters the mouse from hitting its own FX. A's predicted visual stays on screen until timeout after a server-side cooldown rejection, and A gives a less thorough testing and exploit-check plan.
